name: Pluchea

project_scope.note: P. camphorata is the installed comparison anchor under an explicit user-approved range exception. P. odorata remains a source concept outside the canonical manifest in this lane; do not install or promote it from this genus lesson.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Start with the leaves and the architecture of the head clusters. Project Pluchea are glandular/aromatic-looking composites with alternate leaves and many small pink-purple, rayless-looking heads packed into corymbiform or paniculiform arrays.
priority: flat/rounded corymbiform versus more paniculiform head arrays
involucre shape and size for close confirmation

quick_split: P. camphorata — leaves clearly petiolate; stems usually closely arachnose; many small heads arranged in a paniculiform system of rounded-convex corymbiform clusters on ascending bracteate branches.
P. odorata — leaves sessile or petiolate; stems not arachnose; head arrays more directly corymbiform, flat-topped to rounded and often layered.
local_confusers: Heterotheca subaxillaris may share the camphorweed common-name problem but has conspicuous yellow ray florets.
Conoclinium has opposite leaves rather than the alternate Pluchea pattern.

visual_needs: whole flowering P. camphorata showing the overall paniculiform/corymbiform cluster architecture
P. camphorata leaf attachment showing the petiole and glandular surface
closeup of a Pluchea head showing the rayless-looking pink-purple florets and involucre
side-by-side P. camphorata versus P. odorata head-array architecture
side-by-side leaf attachment: clearly petiolate P. camphorata versus the variable sessile/petiolate P. odorata source concept
source_notes: Flora of North America key separates P. camphorata from P. odorata chiefly with stem arachnosity, petiole/leaf attachment, involucre dimensions, and head-array architecture.
